instance.description: HTTPS origin of the user-selected GitHub instance. Ask when the intended instance is unknown.

observe: New review requests, mentions, issue changes and check failures in the selected account or repository. Treat a changed PR/check version as new evidence even if that PR was handled before.
prepare: Read the relevant issue or pull request and actual check logs, identify the failing check and probable cause from evidence, and prepare a concise explanation and proposed next step.
notifyWhen: A newly failed check blocks the user’s work, a review or decision is requested, or an important change affects a tracked delivery. Suppress unchanged failures and unrelated repository activity.

Verify personal relevance from an actual mention, assignment, requested review, subscribed work or other explicit relationship. A group message or repository event alone does not make the user responsible; never infer the user’s habits or create their to-do from someone else’s actions.
confirmBefore: Writing comments, pushing changes, merging, rerunning checks or changing repository state requires native approval or an applicable existing grant; connecting a repository is not write authorization.

instance.description: HTTPS origin of the user-selected GitLab instance. Ask when the intended instance is unknown.

observe: New merge-request review requests, mentions, issue changes and pipeline failures within the selected GitLab instance and resources. Compare object versions rather than treating a handled MR as permanently complete.
prepare: Read the actual merge request, job logs and related discussion, establish the failure or requested decision from evidence, and prepare an actionable summary with source links.
notifyWhen: A new pipeline failure blocks relevant work, a review or decision needs the user, or a material delivery risk changes. Keep unchanged pipeline failures and irrelevant project activity quiet.

Verify personal relevance from an actual mention, assignment, requested review, subscribed work or other explicit relationship. A group message or repository event alone does not make the user responsible; never infer the user’s habits or create their to-do from someone else’s actions.
confirmBefore: Commenting, pushing, merging, retrying jobs or modifying project state requires native approval or a current scoped grant. Access to one GitLab instance never implies access to another.
